prompt: Two coplanar forces of magnitude 12 N and 5 N act simultaneously at a point. Which value CANNOT be the magnitude of the resultant force?

answer.explanation: The maximum possible resultant occurs when the forces are in the same direction: 12 + 5 = 17 N. The minimum possible resultant occurs when they act in opposite directions: 12 - 5 = 7 N. Any angle between 0 degrees and 180 degrees produces a resultant between 7 N and 17 N (for example, 13 N when perpendicular). A magnitude of 6 N is outside this possible range.

distractor_explanations: Correct. 6 N is less than the minimum possible resultant of 12 - 5 = 7 N.
Incorrect. 7 N is the minimum resultant, obtained when the forces act in opposite directions (180 degrees).
Incorrect. 13 N is the resultant when the forces are perpendicular: sqrt(12^2 + 5^2) = 13 N.
Incorrect. 17 N is the maximum resultant, obtained when the forces act in the same direction (0 degrees).
hints: What is the minimum possible magnitude of two combined forces?
What is the maximum possible magnitude?
solution: Minimum resultant = 12 - 5 = 7 N. Maximum resultant = 12 + 5 = 17 N. Since 6 N < 7 N, a resultant of 6 N is impossible. Option 1 is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Determine the range of possible resultant magnitudes: |F1 - F2| <= R <= (F1 + F2).
Step 3: Check options: 7 N, 13 N, 17 N all lie in [7, 17] N.
Step 4: 6 N is outside the range. Choose option 1.
